reforms.description: Japan has implemented a comprehensive programme to promote energy conservation, develop alternative sources of supply, and encourage research and technological improvements in energy policy.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The programme aims to enhance energy efficiency and innovation in energy technologies, which can lead to long-term economic benefits.
reforms.status_evidence: The programme has been implemented to promote energy conservation and technological improvements.
reforms.importance_rationale: The programme represents a significant and comprehensive approach to energy policy and innovation.
reforms.source_quote: Important non-price measures have also been taken, in accordance with specific legislation enacted in recent years, to promote energy conservation, to develop alternative sources of supply and to encourage research and technological improvements.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The description mentions encouraging research and technological improvements in energy policy, indicating a focus on sectoral R&D.

reforms.description: Japan enacted comprehensive energy policy legislation in 1980 to address energy constraints through conservation and alternative energy development. The Alternative Energy Law (May 1980) established a new public corporation to lead technological development and commercialisation of alternative energy sources including coal liquefaction, geothermal, and solar energy, with provision of subsidies, debt guarantees, and loans. The 'Moonlight' project, a government R&D programme focused on energy conservation technologies, received substantial budget increases (over 150% to 8 billion Yen in FY 1980).
reforms.component_name: Alternative Energy Law and Public Corporation
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Energy conservation and alternative energy R&D reduce dependence on imported oil, lowering energy costs and improving allocative efficiency. Applied research in these sectors supports long-term productivity gains and technological capability.
reforms.status_evidence: Alternative Energy Law enacted May 1980; Moonlight project operational in FY 1980. Both legislative enactment and immediate implementation in same fiscal year.
reforms.importance_rationale: Structural, system-wide reform establishing new institutional framework (public corporation) and major budget increases for energy R&D in response to energy crisis. Combines legislative enactment with substantial funding commitment.
reforms.source_quote: The Alternative Energy Law, enacted in May 1980, calls for the MITI Minister to set and publish overall targets for oil substitution... A new public corporation is being established to play a central role in this area. Its main activities include: technological development related to coal liquefaction, geothermal and solar energy; granting of subsidies and debt guarantees for exploration of geothermal energy sources; and loans and debt guarantees for exploration of overseas coal resources.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The reform discusses a government R&D programme focused on energy conservation technologies, which aligns with sectoral R&D efforts.

all_reforms_including_excluded.description: A 10 percent investment tax credit on equipment and machinery was provided to promote structural changes in industry, effective until the end of FY 1980.
all_reforms_including_excluded.growth_orientation_rationale: The investment tax credit incentivizes firms to invest in equipment and machinery, which can enhance productivity and innovation.
all_reforms_including_excluded.status_evidence: The tax credit was effective until the end of FY 1980.
all_reforms_including_excluded.importance_rationale: The reform is a minor adjustment aimed at promoting investment rather than a significant overhaul.
all_reforms_including_excluded.source_quote: A 10 per cent investment tax credit on equipment and machinery was provided to promote structural changes in industry.
all_reforms_including_excluded.cross_verification_note: The reform focuses on a 10 percent investment tax credit on equipment and machinery, which does not directly relate to R&D funding or innovation instruments for firms.
